supporting_observations.claim: The account creation occurred at 13:46 UTC, shortly after the alert's approximate time, and identifies sara.ali as the creator of ext.rwong.
A 13:43 UTC Kerberos network logon for sara.ali came from WS-SALI-01's IP address; the account-creation event carries the same logon ID, linking the creation to that authenticated session.

The account name follows the supplied help-desk temporary-account convention, ext.<name>, and the available membership event adds it to Contractors, consistent with the stated account-creation practice.
The supplied evidence contains no observed use of ext.rwong after creation during the reviewed interval.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records show the account-creation and group-add events, but do not show the process or interface that performed the creation. Relevant records: T128-00032, T128-00033.
The account-creation records do not establish the business request, sponsor, or approval for ext.rwong. Relevant records: T128-00032, T128-00033.
The supplied records do not establish the account's complete group memberships or permissions; T128-00033 records an addition to Contractors, not a complete membership inventory.
claims_not_established: Whether ext.rwong was requested for a specific business purpose or had an approved sponsor.
Whether ext.rwong had any other group memberships or permissions not represented in the supplied records.
Whether the absence of ext.rwong activity in the supplied records means the account was not used elsewhere or outside the reviewed interval.
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: sara.ali launched mstsc.exe to FILE-COP-01 and established a remote interactive logon from WS-SALI-01. The supplied inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-PBECKER-01. The records do not link this session to ext.rwong, so it does not determine this alert. Records: T128-00037, T128-00042, T128-00043.
